FLY TYING / BEGINNERS

How to tie a Zebra Midge

One fly, eight clear steps. Gather the materials, follow each stage, and check the finished shape before you start the next one.

Castward field notes Updated 11 November 2026
At a glance
Pattern
Zebra Midge
Lesson
8 illustrated steps
Goal
Secure wraps • clear eye
Start here

Quick answer

Take one stage at a time. Keep the hook eye clear, use only the material the step needs, and check each tie-in before you move on.

On this page

  1. Lay out the materials
  2. Tie it, one step at a time
  3. Your finished fly
  4. Small mistakes, simple fixes
  5. Common questions

01

Lay out the materials

These sizes are a starting recipe. Test the hook and materials together before you tie a batch.[1]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

PartFor this version
HookSize 18 curved emerger hook
BeadSilver; test fit on your hook
Thread and bodyBlack 70 denier
RibSmall silver wire
02

Tie it, one step at a time

  1. 01

    Fit the bead

    Pass the hook point through the bead’s small hole. Slide the bead to the eye, then clamp the bend.

    Bench tip Test the bead before you start.

  2. 02

    Start the thread

    Anchor black thread just behind the bead. Trim the tag.

    Bench tip Avoid a bulky thread lump.

  3. 03

    Anchor the rib

    Secure the silver wire behind the bead. Bind it down the curved shank.

    Bench tip Keep the wire on one side.

  4. 04

    Shape the taper

    Work the thread back and forth, with more wraps near the bead.

    Bench tip Keep the rear slender.

  5. 05

    Smooth the body

    Flatten the thread and cover the ridges with close turns.

    Bench tip Untwist your thread as needed.

  6. 06

    Wind the rib

    Spiral the wire toward the bead in even gaps.

    Bench tip Leave black body visible between turns.

  7. 07

    Secure the wire

    Bind the wire behind the bead. Brace it and twist away the excess.

    Bench tip Protect your fine scissors from the wire.

  8. 08

    Finish the collar

    Whip finish behind the bead. Cut the thread.

    Bench tip Keep the collar small.

[1]
03

Your finished fly

  • ✓The hook eye stays clear.
  • ✓The materials stay put under a gentle tug.
  • ✓The point and hook gap remain usable.
04

Small mistakes, simple fixes

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

What you seeTry this
A bead that jamsTest bead and hook together before you tie.
A lumpy bodyBuild a taper, then cover it with flatter thread.
Heavy ribbingLeave visible black gaps between turns.
A few good questions

Before you head out

Can I change the color?

Yes. Keep the same sequence and use comparable materials. Change one feature at a time so you can see its effect.

What if the fly looks uneven?

Check the secure wraps and open eye first. Keep this fly as a reference, then repeat the recipe with less material.
